events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.55)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the metered distance fare is affected by extra kilometres and RD-2 can yield a partial refund rather than the fixed-quote treatment [F7][RD-2]. The trace records one off-route segment, 21:26–21:37, 6.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, adding 4.89 km [F3][RD-1].

The driver asked before the segment: at 21:23 he asked "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Balestier Road?" and the rider replied at 21:24 "Can lah, go ahead." — a rider message sent before the segment started at 21:26 [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. Being asked "go round via Balestier Road" and answering "can" is agreement to a specific named road, i.e. the named-road branch of RD-5, not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation [F8][F9][RD-5].

For a specific named road, RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to that road; timing alone does not suffice, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record places the car on Balestier Road during 21:26–21:37: the only traffic facts name Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road, and none of them is tied by any fact to the off-route segment [F12][F13][F14][F3][RD-5]. The driver's assertion that he "asked the rider before turning off via Balestier Road" is his own post-trip statement and cannot itself establish consent or the route driven [F11][RD-5]. The record therefore does not settle whether the agreed road is the road driven: G13 applies and the finding is undetermined [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

The traffic record does not exempt the segment on its own: Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road were free-flowing (bands 4 and 5) and there is no incident near the route, while the Central Expressway band-2 record is a corridor record that does not on its own excuse deviation, and in any case no record ties it to the replaced optimal stretch [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. RD-6's account flag is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F18][RD-6]. RD-3 is not the applicable branch because no rider-named stop was involved — the rider named no place, and the driver, not the rider, proposed the road [F8][F9][RD-3(a)].

Safety screen: I read the chat, the complaint and the driver's statement; the messages concern a traffic jam and a proposed route, and nothing in them is a threat, insult, intimidation, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][F12][RD-5] — screening under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 raises nothing [SAFE-1].

Because the undetermined segment finding controls whether any amount is refundable, this case cannot be auto-decided: escalate for a human to establish which road the 21:26–21:37 stretch was driven on. If it was Balestier Road, the rider-concurred deviation is exempt and no refund is due; if it was not, the 4.89 extra km are non-exempt and the trace formula gives 4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.895, i.e. $6.89 refund_partial [F3][F4][F8][F9][RD-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human reviewer: obtain the router path/road names for 21:26–21:37 and determine whether the 6.64 km stretch was driven on Balestier Road; if it was not, apply RD-2 (4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.89) as refund_partial.

proposed_ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human reviewer: obtain the router path/road names for 21:26–21:37 and determine whether the 6.64 km stretch was driven on Balestier Road; if it was not, apply RD-2 (4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.89) as refund_partial.
proposed_ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the metered distance fare is affected by extra kilometres and RD-2 can yield a partial refund rather than the fixed-quote treatment [F7][RD-2]. The trace records one off-route segment, 21:26–21:37, 6.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, adding 4.89 km [F3][RD-1].

The driver asked before the segment: at 21:23 he asked "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Balestier Road?" and the rider replied at 21:24 "Can lah, go ahead." — a rider message sent before the segment started at 21:26 [F8][F9][F3][RD-5]. Being asked "go round via Balestier Road" and answering "can" is agreement to a specific named road, i.e. the named-road branch of RD-5, not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation [F8][F9][RD-5].

For a specific named road, RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to that road; timing alone does not suffice, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. Nothing in the record places the car on Balestier Road during 21:26–21:37: the only traffic facts name Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road, and none of them is tied by any fact to the off-route segment [F12][F13][F14][F3][RD-5]. The driver's assertion that he "asked the rider before turning off via Balestier Road" is his own post-trip statement and cannot itself establish consent or the route driven [F11][RD-5]. The record therefore does not settle whether the agreed road is the road driven: G13 applies and the finding is undetermined [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

The traffic record does not exempt the segment on its own: Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road were free-flowing (bands 4 and 5) and there is no incident near the route, while the Central Expressway band-2 record is a corridor record that does not on its own excuse deviation, and in any case no record ties it to the replaced optimal stretch [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. RD-6's account flag is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F18][RD-6]. RD-3 is not the applicable branch because no rider-named stop was involved — the rider named no place, and the driver, not the rider, proposed the road [F8][F9][RD-3(a)].

Safety screen: I read the chat, the complaint and the driver's statement; the messages concern a traffic jam and a proposed route, and nothing in them is a threat, insult, intimidation, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][F12][RD-5] — screening under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 raises nothing [SAFE-1].

Because the undetermined segment finding controls whether any amount is refundable, this case cannot be auto-decided: escalate for a human to establish which road the 21:26–21:37 stretch was driven on. If it was Balestier Road, the rider-concurred deviation is exempt and no refund is due; if it was not, the 4.89 extra km are non-exempt and the trace formula gives 4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.895, i.e. $6.89 refund_partial [F3][F4][F8][F9][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's request for no_action relies on the 21:24 agreement 'Can lah, go ahead.' [F9], but that agreement is to a named road and nothing in the record ties the 21:26–21:37 off-route segment of 6.64 km (4.89 km extra, up to 2070 m off the optimal route) to that road; timing alone cannot establish it and the driver's post-trip statement is not consent [F3][F8][F11][RD-5].

The driver's position of no_action rests on the pre-detour agreement [F8][F9], but the mere fact that a rider message precedes the segment does not show the segment was driven on the agreed road; no fact places the car on Balestier Road during the segment, and his own statement asserting it is a claim, not consent or route evidence [F3][F11][RD-5].

Any claim that congestion excused the deviation fails: there is no qualifying incident, Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road were at bands 4–5 (free-flowing), and a speed band alone cannot exempt the segment nor is it tied to the replaced optimal stretch [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 21:26:50 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F8: Chat #1 21:23 driver: “Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Balestier Road?”; F9: Chat #2 21:24 rider: “Can lah, go ahead.”; F11: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked the rider before turning off via Balestier Road and the rider said can.” (F8, F9, F11)

A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. No stop measured in this segment. (F8, F9)
